what_worked: Unusually disciplined separation of observed dataset facts from illustrative estimates, with honest caveats throughout.
fix_next: Top-10 revenue share is 49.6%, not 50.6%; the $133.8m 'verified 12-month card volume' figure has no clear derivation from the 30-day dataset total.
verdict: Strong thesis built on real data, but key headline numbers don't reconcile cleanly.
factual_error_detail: Slide 4: Top-10 share stated as 50.6%, reference is 49.6%. Slide 3: $133.8m '12-month card volume' — dataset is 30-day ($15.6M); annualizing gives ~$187M, not $133.8M; unclear filter or derivation. Slide 5: Stripe share of volume 90.9% vs reference 86.7% ($13.5M/$15.6M); may reflect a different denominator but is not explained.

evidence.insight: Slide 6 'quality of book not size of book' is a genuinely original cut — comparing % of accounts above $10k MRR across providers. Slide 9 identifies 14% MoR switchers carrying only 1.8% of volume as a wedge signal. Slide 14 comparison table synthesizes dataset observations into a strategic contrast.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc: market context (slides 2-6) → compliance wedge thesis (7-9) → NRI corridor opportunity (10-12) → solution (13-14) → ask (15) → caveats (16). Each section builds on the prior. The thesis — compliance, not checkout, is the next value layer — is sustained throughout.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 explicitly flags missingness rates (country 76%, category 73%), marks NRI figures as illustrative estimates, and distinguishes dataset from external sources. Slide 16 dedicates an entire page to caveats. Audience (seed investors) and scope are clear from slide 1.
evidence.accuracy: Top-10 share off by ~1 percentage point (50.6% vs 49.6%). The $133.8m figure doesn't reconcile with the dataset total ($15.6M × 12 ≈ $187M) — some unstated filter may be applied but it's not disclosed. Stripe volume share 90.9% doesn't match reference 86.7%. Provider account shares are roughly consistent. Median/mean distinction on slide 4 is correctly noted. Country/category missingness percentages are correct (76% = 759/1000, 73% = 726/1000).
evidence.visual: Clean dark theme with consistent section labels, orange accent hierarchy, and restrained chart use. Slide 4 bar chart is clear with annotations. Slide 6 bar chart with cohort average line is effective. Two section-divider slides (7, 10) are pure decoration. Table on slide 5 is legible. No chart junk, but also only two actual charts in 16 slides — mostly text-heavy.
evidence.ai_slop: none — the deck reads as genuinely authored with domain-specific knowledge of Indian financial regulation (NRE/NRO accounts, SEBI, FATCA/CRS, PIS/LRS). No generic filler or decorative meaningless graphics.
